1 Firebase Console setup

🔥 Goal of this step: register your Android app in a Firebase project, turn on App Distribution, and create a tester group.

Open Firebase Console

1) Create or select a project

  1. Click "Add project" or pick an existing one
  2. Enter a project name → accept the terms → "Continue"
  3. Google Analytics is optional (fine to leave on)

2) Register the Android app

⚠️ Pick the Android icon, not the Flutter one

The add-app screen shows a Flutter option, but it leads to the flutterfire configure CLI flow that integrates the Firebase SDK into your app.

App Distribution only needs the APK upload, so no SDK integration is required. Register with the Android icon (🤖).

  1. Click Project Overview at the top left
  2. Among the add-app icons, choose Android (🤖)
  3. Android package name (e.g. kr.mycompany.myapp)
    Must match applicationId in android/app/build.gradle.kts
  4. You can leave the SHA-1 certificate fingerprint empty (not needed for App Distribution)
  5. Click Register app → download google-services.json → upload it in Step 4
  6. Skip the SDK setup screens that follow
    The "Add Firebase SDK" and "Next steps" screens aren't needed if you only use App Distribution.
  7. From "gear icon → Project settings" at the bottom left, copy the App ID (e.g. 1:905...:android:abc) → used in Step 3

3) Turn on App Distribution

⚠️ Skip this and deployments fail with 404

Even with the app registered and permissions granted, the upload API returns 404 Requested entity was not found until App Distribution itself is turned on. It is easy to mistake for a permission problem, so check it.

  1. Left menu → "Release & Monitor" → "App Distribution"
  2. Click "Get started" → it's on
  3. Once it's on, the "Testers & Groups" tab appears — that is the success signal

4) Create a tester group

  1. App Distribution → top tab "Testers & Groups"
  2. Click "Add group" on the left → enter a group name (e.g. testers)
  3. Add tester emails to the group
    Adding them only to "All testers" won't reach the group. Put them inside the group.

⚠️ Step 3 needs the "group alias", not the "display name"

Firebase stores the name you typed as a separate lowercase alias. Deployments use the alias.

Display name : AcmeTeam
Actual alias : acmeteam ← use this

Click the group: the value at the end of the address bar URL is the alias. If case or spaces differ, deployment fails with group not found.

Already done →

2 Create the service account + grant access Important

🔑 Why? GitHub Actions needs credentials to upload builds to Firebase. The Service Account JSON key provides them.

Open Cloud Console — Service Accounts Open Cloud Console — IAM

1) Create the service account

  1. Click the "Service Accounts" button above
  2. Select the project at the top → make sure it's the same project as Firebase
  3. Click "+ Create service account"
  4. Name: firebase-app-distribution-uploader (example)
  5. "Create and continue" → you can leave the role empty for now → "Done"

💡 A key from the Firebase Console works too

A firebase-adminsdk-* key from Firebase Console → Project settings → Service accounts tab → "Generate new private key" also works.

⚠️ But that key does not get App Distribution access automatically. Be sure to do the IAM step (3) below.

⚠️ You can't reuse a key from another project

Even if you have a Play Store deployment key, it won't work for a different Firebase project. A service account belongs to its project and has no access to other projects' resources.

2) Create the JSON key

  1. Click the service account row you just created
  2. Top tab "Keys" → "Add key" → "Create new key" → choose JSON → "Create"
  3. The JSON file downloads automatically (upload it in Step 4)
  4. ⚠️ The downloaded JSON is highly sensitive. Don't commit it to Git. Remember where you saved it.

3) Grant IAM access

  1. Click the "IAM" button above
  2. On the row of the service account email you just created (...@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com), click the pencil icon on the right
  3. "+ Add another role" → search roles → choose "Firebase App Distribution Admin"
  4. "Save" → access granted

✅ Verification checklist

🔍 Check before deploying (recommended)

The commands below check the actual access. If they fail here, deployment fails too.

# If you have the gcloud CLI
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=key-file.json
gcloud projects get-iam-policy PROJECT_ID --flatten="bindings[].members" \
  --filter="bindings.members:$(python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(open('key-file.json'))['client_email'])")"
Tell the cause from the response code:
• 403 permission denied → IAM role not granted (item 3 above)
• 404 not found → App Distribution not turned on (Step 1, item 3)
• 200 OK → all good, ready to deploy

3 Enter app info

📋 Enter the App ID and tester group you found in Step 1. They are used to fill in the placeholders in your workflow files.

Firebase Console → Project settings → Your apps → App ID

App Distribution → Testers & Groups → group alias

⚠️ It's the lowercase alias, not the display name you see on screen (e.g. display AcmeTeam → enter acmeteam)

⚙️ Command that fills in the workflow placeholders

Copy the command for your OS → run it from the project root. The setup script is included in the Step 5 ZIP.

python3 .github/util/flutter/firebase-wizard/firebase-wizard.py setup --project-path . --app-id "" --tester-group ""
python .github\util\flutter\firebase-wizard\firebase-wizard.py setup --project-path . --app-id "" --tester-group ""
